## Question 1

Load the patchwork package. Create three plots from `mpg` and save them as objects `p1`, `p2`, `p3`: a scatterplot of `displ` vs `hwy`, a boxplot of `hwy` by `drv`, and a bar chart of `class`. Compose them with patchwork operators:

- `p1 | p2` (side by side)
- `p1 / p2` (stacked)
- `(p1 | p2) / p3` (two on top, one below)

Write one sentence explaining what `|` and `/` each do.

## Question 2

Make two scatterplots from `mpg` that share the same colour mapping (`colour = drv`): `displ` vs `hwy` and `displ` vs `cty`. Place them side by side, first with a plain `p1 | p2`, then with

```r
(p1 | p2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

Write one sentence describing what `guides = "collect"` changed and why the collected version is better when the two legends are identical.

## Question 3

Take your composition from Question 2 and add an overall title and panel tags with `plot_annotation()`:

```r
(p1 | p2) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(title = "Fuel economy and engine size",
                  tag_levels = "a")
```

Write one sentence on why panel tags such as "(a)" and "(b)" are standard practice in academic figures.
